cases.name: Patrina Sharmaine Best
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Patrina was proud of her Bajan and Filipino heritage, and always loved the beach. She was a standout swimmer from an early age and went on to swim competitively at Camden County High School and Georgia Southern University. She excelled at sprint freestyle, and her best event was the 100 breaststroke, in which she garnered All-Conference honors while at GSU. She worked as a lifeguard throughout college and had a passion for teaching children to swim. After completing her college swimming career, she continued her athletic pursuits with CrossFit. She competed in CrossFit events from Virginia to Hawaii and was known for her impressive strength and agility, along with her radiant smile and encouraging personality in the gym.

After college graduation in 2008, she worked briefly as an exercise physiologist before pursuing her true passion and becoming a registered nurse in the operating room. Patrina worked as an OR nurse in Fairfax, VA and then traveled the country as a travel OR nurse during the COVID-19 pandemic. She loved providing expert nursing care to communities in dire need of qualified OR nurses. Patrina was born into a US Navy family, and always had a love of travel, which continued as an adult. Her travels included the Philippines, Korea, Japan, Vietnam, Thailand, Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia, Iceland and most of Europe, as well as Barbados, much of the Caribbean, Mexico and across the United States. Some of her other favorite activities included fitness, thrifting, exploring new restaurants, going to the beach, paddleboarding, Scrabble, Legos and cheering for her beloved Jacksonville Jaguars and GSU Eagles. She loved to play ball with her cherished West Highland Terrier, Luke, or to cuddle with him on the couch. Most of all, Patrina loved to spend time with her family, whether at home or traveling together around the globe.

Patrina was always quick to laugh and slow to anger. She had the most beautiful smile and shared it easily with everyone around her. She was known for being fun-loving and friendly. Her joy and light were infectious. She was independent and strong, but also deeply compassionate and sensitive. Above all, she was dependable and a wonderful friend. She was a beautiful person, inside and out, and made an impact on many people around the world. She will be forever missed, yet her memory and light will live on in the world forever."

Best's family remembered her as a “fun-loving, warm-hearted person [who] made friends easily everywhere she went.”

They said as the daughter of a U.S. Navy chief petty officer, Best lived all over the world before she graduated from high school in Georgia and then earned her nursing degree.

“Patrina was a constant source of joy and laughter in our lives. She was guaranteed to be present for every birthday, holiday, and special occasion,” the Best family said in a statement to News4. “She was a wonderful person in every regard. She was the light of our lives, and we will miss her dearly for the rest of our days.”

Best leaves behind her parents, her “best friend” and older sister Gianina Best, her brother-in-law, and a niece and nephew “who consider her the greatest ‘Tita’ in the entire world. She also leaves behind her beloved dog, Luke, who traveled with her to every location she worked as a travel nurse,” her family said.
cases.narrative: On 2/17/2024, she was found dead inside her parents' home in the 800 block of St. James Court in Accokeek, MD authorities said. Her boyfriend turned himself in to police after strangling her that morning, police said.
